lines.text: Restaurants track pour cost: ingredient cost divided by the drink's price.
lines.say: Restaurants track pour cost: ingredient cost divided by the drink's price.

lines.text: Industry guides say bars aim for 18-24%. Kitchens, 28-35%.
lines.say: Industry guides say bars aim for eighteen to twenty-four percent. Kitchens, twenty-eight to thirty-five.

lines.text: Example: a drink and a burger both cost $12. At 20%, the drink leaves $9.60. At 30%, the burger leaves $8.40.
lines.say: Say a drink and a burger both cost twelve dollars. At twenty percent, the drink leaves nine dollars and sixty cents. At thirty percent, the burger leaves eight dollars and forty cents.

lines.text: That's $1.20 more, before staff or rent.

lines.text: Food keeps climbing, too: ground beef averaged $6.92 a pound in August 2026.

post.ig:
Why is McDonald's betting big on drinks?
In Sept 2026, McDonald's told investors its specialty drinks are high margin.
Industry guides say bars aim for an 18-24% pour cost; kitchens aim for 28-35% food cost. Example: a $12 drink at 20% leaves $9.60, a $12 burger at 30% leaves $8.40.
Ground beef averaged $6.92/lb in Aug 2026 (BLS). Flanigan's FY2025 10-K: liquor stores 25.1% gross margin, restaurants (food and bar) 66.6%.
Sources: McDonald's Investor Day 2026; BLS average prices; Flanigan's FY2025 10-K; industry pour-cost guides.
